context: Icicle (partition) chart of a synthetic ~500-file project tree with 4 depth levels (root → 8 dirs → subdirs → files), linked to a log-scale brushable histogram of file sizes below; 7-color TOL palette keyed to top-level directories; click-to-zoom and breadcrumb navigation.
first_impression: Reads clearly at the directory levels, but the file-level bottom row degrades into illegible hairline slivers that create visual noise across the right half of the chart.
what_works: The 7-color palette maps cleanly to top-level directories and propagates consistently through all depth levels, making it easy to track which subtree belongs to which parent; the two-view layout (icicle + histogram) is minimal and the brush-linking between them is intuitive without competing for attention.
what_doesnt: The deepest file-level row collapses into dozens of near-zero-width slivers that are visually indistinguishable and unlabeled, making the bottom third of the icicle read as noise rather than information; the full-width gray root band consumes roughly 15% of the icicle height while conveying only the word 'project', wasting prime real estate that could expand the readable directory rows.
